title: Citraturic response to oral citric acid load
authors: Sakhaee K, Alpern R, Poindexter J, Pak CY
followUp: 4 hours after a single oral load
population: Normal adult men and women (PubMed indexing)
funder: Not read: the full text returned HTTP 403 from the publisher and the AUA journal pages, no archived copy was found, and the abstract carries no funding statement. PubMed lists NIH grants M01-RR00633 (NCRR) and P01-DK20543 (NIDDK).
result: From the PubMed abstract: single oral load of 40 mEq citric acid in 6 normal subjects, compared with a control phase without drug, with serum and urinary citrate measured for 4 hours. Serum citrate rose significantly (p < 0.05) 30 minutes after the load and remained raised for 3 hours; urinary citrate excretion peaked at 2 hours and fell over the next 2 hours; differences between phases were significant at 2 and 3 hours. Urinary pH, carbon dioxide pressure, bicarbonate, total carbon dioxide and ammonium, serum electrolytes, and arterialised venous pH and carbon dioxide pressure did not change. The authors conclude that the citratemic and citraturic effects are largely accountable by absorbed citrate that escaped degradation.
